Remark Formal proof of the V_{(3)} per-irrep character difference closed form: \chi_{(3)}(\beta_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\beta_p) = -(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)/(4q) = -(q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1})/4, with explicit \varepsilon^k pattern via polynomial + geometric decomposition. Formal proof of the V_{(3)} per-irrep character difference closed form.

  \boxed{
    \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
    \;=\; -\frac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q}
    \;=\; -\frac{q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1}}{4}
  }

Derivation

On V_{(3)} (the symmetric 1-dimensional irrep of H_3(q)), each Hecke generator acts as the scalar q:

  • \sigma_i \mapsto q
  • \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}) \mapsto q^{-1}
  • \text{averaged} = \frac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}) \mapsto (q + q^{-1})/2

The canonical typed-\mathbf{B}_3 braids carry:

  • \mathcal{B}_p (uud): 6\sigma + 3\sigma^{-1} + 2\text{ averaged}
  • \mathcal{B}_n (udd): 5\sigma + 4\sigma^{-1} + 2\text{ averaged}

The characters multiply as:

  • \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p) = q^6 \cdot q^{-3} \cdot \left(\frac{q + q^{-1}}{2}\right)^2 = q^3 \cdot \frac{(q + q^{-1})^2}{4}
  • \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) = q^5 \cdot q^{-4} \cdot \left(\frac{q + q^{-1}}{2}\right)^2 = q \cdot \frac{(q + q^{-1})^2}{4}

The difference factors as:

  \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
  = (q - q^3) \cdot \frac{(q + q^{-1})^2}{4}
  = -q(q^2 - 1) \cdot \frac{(q^2 + 1)^2/q^2}{4}
  = -\frac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q}.

Expanding the rational form gives:

  -\frac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q}
  = -\frac{(q^4 + 2q^2 + 1)(q^2 - 1)}{4q}
  = -\frac{q^6 + q^4 - q^2 - 1}{4q}
  = -\frac{q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1}}{4}.

Pattern at q = 1 + \varepsilon

The closed form splits into polynomial and geometric components:

  -\frac{q^5 + q^3 - q - q^{-1}}{4}
   \;=\; \underbrace{-\frac{q^5 + q^3 - q}{4}}_{\text{polynomial part (degree 5)}}
       \;+\; \underbrace{\frac{q^{-1}}{4}}_{\text{geometric series part}}.
  • The polynomial part has degree 5 in q. Its \varepsilon^k coefficient at q = 1 + \varepsilon vanishes for k \geq 6.
  • The geometric part \frac{q^{-1}}{4} = \frac{1}{4(1 + \varepsilon)} = \frac{1}{4} \sum_{k \geq 0} (-1)^k \varepsilon^k contributes \frac{(-1)^k}{4} at every order k.

For k \geq 6, one therefore has:

  [\varepsilon^k]\;\bigl(\chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)\bigr)\big|_{q = 1 + \varepsilon}
   \;=\; \frac{(-1)^k}{4}.

Three closed forms

For the canonical typed-\mathbf{B}_3 braids \mathcal{B}_p (uud, 6\sigma + 3\sigma^{-1} + 2\ \mathrm{averaged}) and \mathcal{B}_n (udd, 5\sigma + 4\sigma^{-1} + 2\ \mathrm{averaged}), the per-Wedderburn-block character differences are:

\begin{aligned}
  \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   &= -\dfrac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q}, \\[6pt]
  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   &= -\dfrac{(q^4 + 1)(q^2 - 1)}{4 q^3}, \\[6pt]
  \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   &= -\dfrac{(q^2 + 1)^2 (q^2 - 1)}{4 q^5}.
\end{aligned}

All three have the common prefactor -\frac{(q^2 - 1)}{4 \cdot q^{?}} where the denominator power is 1, 3, 5 for \lambda = (3), (2,1), (1,1,1).

Cyclotomic factorisation

See Table 1.

Recall: \Phi_1(q) = q-1, \Phi_2(q) = q+1, \Phi_4(q) = q^2+1, \Phi_8(q) = q^4+1.

Two observations:

  1. V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} share the identical numerator polynomial — only the denominator differs (q vs q^5). The denominator-power gap of 4 exactly matches the factor by which the closed forms differ:

    \chi_{(1,1,1)}\text{-diff}(q) = \frac{\chi_{(3)}\text{-diff}(q)}{q^4}.

    This manifests the conjugate-partition symmetry: (1,1,1) forms the conjugate (transpose) of (3). The corresponding sign-rep \leftrightarrow trivial-rep duality (\sigma_i \mapsto q vs \sigma_i \mapsto -q^{-1}) produces the q \leftrightarrow -q^{-1} substitution that maps the two characters into each other.

  2. V_{(2,1)} involves 8th roots of unity (\Phi_8 = q^4 + 1, whose roots form the primitive 8th roots). V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} involve 4th roots (\Phi_4 = q^2 + 1). This structure aligns with the Clifford depth of the H_3 representations: V_{(2,1)} forms the 2-d Hoefsmit irrep (Cl(3) depth), while the 1-d irreps V_{(3)}, V_{(1,1,1)} form Cl(2) depth.

  3. Denominator power tracks the content sum:

    • c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i)
    • c((3)) = 0+1+2 = 3, denominator q
    • c((2,1)) = 0+1-1 = 0, denominator q^3
    • c((1,1,1)) = 0-1-2 = -3, denominator q^5

    The denominator exponent obeys p = 3 - \frac{2}{3} c(\lambda), mapping c \in \{3, 0, -3\} to p \in \{1, 3, 5\} exactly.

Origin of the V_(2,1) closed form

V_(2,1) is the 2-dimensional Hoefsmit irrep. Each typed crossing acts as a 2\times2 matrix on the SYT basis \{v_{T_1}, v_{T_2}\}:

  • \sigma_0 \mapsto \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) (diagonal, eigenvalues q and -q^{-1})
  • \sigma_1 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} d_1 & b \\ b & d_2 \end{pmatrix} with d_1 = q^3/(q^2 + 1), d_2 = -q^{-1}/(q^2 + 1), b = \sqrt{d_1 d_2 + 1}
  • \sigma_i^{-1} \mapsto \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1}) I
  • averaged \mapsto \frac{1}{2}(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1})

The character \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta) = \mathrm{Tr}\bigl(\prod_{c \in \beta} M_c\bigr) where M_c is the matrix for each crossing in the canonical word order of the atomic braid.

Per-Wedderburn-block leading-order pattern: dimension-scaled Hopf-Jones absorption

Expanding the per-block character closed forms (from All three V_\lambda per-irrep character difference closed forms with cyclotomic factor pattern) around q = 1 in \varepsilon = q - 1 exposes a structural pattern in the \varepsilon^1 leading-order coefficients.

V_{(3)} -\dfrac{(q^2+1)^2(q^2-1)}{4q} \mathbf{-2} Full (= J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1))
V_{(2,1)} -\dfrac{(q^4+1)(q^2-1)}{4q^3} -1 Half (= J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1)/2)

Structural interpretation

Each block is linear in \hbar_q = (q-1)/q at leading order. Factoring out the common (q^2-1) = q(q+1)\hbar_q gives:

\begin{aligned}
\chi_{(3)}(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p)     &= -\tfrac{1}{4}(q^2+1)^2 (q+1) \cdot \hbar_q, \\[4pt]
\chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p)   &= -\tfrac{1}{4q^2}(q^4+1) (q+1) \cdot \hbar_q, \\[4pt]
\chi_{(1,1,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p) &= -\tfrac{1}{4q^4}(q^2+1)^2 (q+1) \cdot \hbar_q.
\end{aligned}

One extracts the leading-order \varepsilon^1 = 2\hbar_q\big|_{q=1} coefficients by setting q = 1 in the cyclotomic factor:

  • V_{(3)}: -\tfrac{1}{4}(2)^2 \cdot 2 = -2 = J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1).
  • V_{(2,1)}: -\tfrac{1}{4}(2) \cdot 2 = -1 = J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1)/2.
  • V_{(1,1,1)}: -\tfrac{1}{4}(2)^2 \cdot 2 = -2 = J_{\text{Hopf}}(q{=}1).

The one-dimensional representations (V_{(3)} trivial, V_{(1,1,1)} sign) absorb the full Hopf-Jones value -2. The two-dimensional standard representation V_{(2,1)} absorbs half, -1. The character-formula scaling by \dim(V_\lambda) accounts for this halving.

Connection to c_3 = -2

Both one-dimensional representations absorb -2 in full. The two-dimensional representation absorbs -1, but carries a character-formula multiplicity \dim V_{(2,1)} = 2 in the Wedderburn sum. The dimension-weighted sum reproduces the global c_3 before Wenzl-bridge re-weighting via y_\lambda:

\dim_q^2(V_{(3)}) (-2) + \dim_q^2(V_{(2,1)}) (-1/2) + \dim_q^2(V_{(1,1,1)}) (-2)

Evaluating at q = 1 yields 1 (-2) + 4 (-1/2) + 1 (-2) = -6.

Under the Markov-bridge y_\lambda weighting, y_\lambda at q=1 satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(1)=1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma)=z=1/2, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2)=z^2=1/4. This yields y_{(3)}(1)=1/2, y_{(2,1)}(1)=1/4, and y_{(1,1,1)}(1)=0. The sum evaluates to:

y_{(3)}(1) (-2) + y_{(2,1)}(1) (-1) + y_{(1,1,1)}(1) (-2) = -\tfrac{5}{4}.

This provides the Markov-trace leading-order coefficient \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p) \approx -\tfrac{5}{4}\varepsilon + O(\varepsilon^2). At the aether parameter q_0, the y_\lambda values constitute q-dependent rational functions rather than a probability measure. A direct computation gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_n - \mathcal{B}_p) \approx -0.142, consistent with the y_\lambda(q_0) \chi_\lambda(q_0) sum.

Significance

This per-block absorption pattern establishes the foundation for extending the coefficient sequence beyond c_3. Higher precision-ladder coefficients c_k for k \geq 4 arise from products of the per-block linear-in-\hbar_q factors, producing \hbar_q^k at order k. Each block's contribution carries the leading-order Hopf-Jones absorption, modulated by the block's cyclotomic-factor structure (\Phi_4^2 for one-dimensional representations; \Phi_8 for two-dimensional representations).

  \chi_{(3)}(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q)

  \;=\; -\frac{(q^2 - 1)(q^2 + 1)^2}{4q^5}.

Only \chi_{(2,1)} depends on the order in which the two nucleon strands are braided, and it is the only two-dimensional block. In V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} the generators act by scalars, so they commute and the intra-nucleon ordering cannot reach those characters: the two orderings give literally the same rational function there. Each block vanishes at the classical point q = 1. The antipode pairing relates the sign and trivial representations for all q > 0:

  \chi_{(1,1,1)}(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q)
  \;=\; q^{-4} \chi_{(3)}(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q).

  y_{(2,1)}(q) = \tfrac{1}{2} - z(q), \qquad
  y_{(1,1,1)}(q) = z(q),

where z(q) = \sqrt q / (1 + q) = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}) is an auxiliary algebraic function used solely to inhabit this hypothesis (distinct from the Markov parameter q^3/(q^2+1)); it witnesses that the normalisation condition is non-empty, and nothing downstream identifies this auxiliary z(q) with the paper's Markov parameter.

Cross-references

  • Class declaration: Per-block character closed forms for \chi_\lambda(\Delta_{T_\beta})(q) over H_3(q) §Extension #4.

prf:qbeta-canonical-markov-weights-expli:
Proof Proof of qbeta canonical markov weights explicit instance.

y_{(3)}(q) + 2 \, y_{(2,1)}(q) + y_{(1,1,1)}(q)
= z(q) + 2 \left( \tfrac{1}{2} - z(q) \right) + z(q)
= 1

This holds for every q > 0. \square

Scope of the explicit choice

This explicitly constructs weights satisfying the canonical Markov-weight hypothesis. It establishes that:

  • The hypothesis is satisfiable.
  • The conditional results stated under it (specifically the canonical (q^2-1) factor of the Markov trace difference and its corollary, vanishing at q = 1) are not vacuous.
  • The hypothesis accommodates the archimedean \sqrt q parametrization of this auxiliary choice alongside the rational Wenzl–Markov weights at z = q^3/(q^2+1).

It does not establish:

  • That this instance is the canonical Wenzl–Markov weights. The canonical weights from H_3(q) have a specific closed form derived from the Hecke algebra's Bratteli diagram and quantum dimensions. They are tied to the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot \sigma_{n-1}) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{n-1}(q). The canonical inhabitant is identified in the next section.
  • A formula for \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M^{\text{can}}(q) at this instance, though it is computable from the canonical (q^2 - 1) factorisation.
  • Any bearing on the c_k ladder closure.

The canonical inhabitant, identified

The canonical choice carries the production trace's own weights:

  y_{(3)} = \frac{[4]_q}{[2]_q^{3}} = \frac{q^4+1}{(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  y_{(2,1)} = \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}} = \frac{q^2}{(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  y_{(1^3)} = 0 .

Why these weights are canonical. The Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the N=2 member of the Ocneanu family z_N = q^N/[N]_q — its framing ratio a^2 = z/z_- is the monomial q^4, which collapses every Ocneanu numerator into quantum integers and turns the weight product into the hook-content formula w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{sl}_N})/[N]_q^{\,n} (see Reconciliation of the Markov parameter z). Thus the three values are derived from the trace rather than chosen to satisfy the normalisation, and the vanishing y_{(1^3)} = 0 is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 row bound ([0]_q = 0 at content -2).

Derived from the Markov axioms. The three values equal the unique n = 3 Markov weights solved from \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1) = q^3/(q^2+1), and the Markov relation, matching the n = 3 slice of the general-n Ocneanu formula (Reconciliation of the Markov parameter z).

The normalisation is an identity, not a constraint that had to be arranged. The normalisation y_{(3)} + 2y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} = 1 reduces to (q^4+1) + 2q^2 = (q^2+1)^2, which holds for every q with no positivity hypothesis — equivalently [4]_q = ([2]_q^2 - 2)[2]_q, so [4]_q/[2]_q^3 = 1 - 2/[2]_q^2.

The explicit \sqrt q-bearing choice is not wrong. It satisfies the normalisation because z + 2(\tfrac12 - z) + z = 1 for any z — which is precisely why it satisfies the hypothesis without being the production weights. It differs from the canonical set on all three blocks.

Numerical sanity check

At the aether parameter q = q_0 \approx 1.10998, the auxiliary function evaluates to \sqrt{q_0} / (1 + q_0) \approx 0.499 (distinct from the Markov parameter q_0^3/(q_0^2+1) \approx 0.6127), yielding y_{(3)}(q_0) \approx 0.499, y_{(2,1)}(q_0) \approx 0.001, and y_{(1,1,1)}(q_0) \approx 0.499, with 0.499 + 2(0.001) + 0.499 = 1.000.

By contrast, the canonical Wenzl–Markov weights at q_0 (for z = q^3/(q^2+1)) are y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3 \approx 0.5054042, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2 \approx 0.2472979, and y_{(1^3)} = 0, satisfying \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 with d = (1, 2, 1) and zero truncation residue.

The difference between the auxiliary witness and the canonical Wenzl–Markov weights is concentrated on the mixed and alternating blocks: while on the symmetric block (3) the auxiliary value y_{(3)} = z(q_0) \approx 0.4993 differs from the canonical \approx 0.5054 by \approx 1.2\,\%, on the remaining blocks the explicit choice gives y_{(2,1)} \approx 0.0007 against the canonical \approx 0.2473, and y_{(1,1,1)} \approx 0.4993 where the canonical weight vanishes identically. The hypothesis admits infinitely many algebraic solutions; the explicit choice witnesses its non-vacuity over \mathbb{R}, whereas the canonical choice supplies the unique Wenzl–Ocneanu weights of the production trace.
prose:intro-hecke-baer-star-chirality: The Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} on H_n(q) induces a Baer-* involution on the centralizer algebra that pairs each Young partition \lambda with its transpose \lambda' while fixing self-conjugate diagrams \lambda = \lambda'. This section establishes the generic Baer-* structure, formulates the Murphy–Lagrange central idempotents in terms of Jucys–Murphy content interpolation, and shows how the chirality period pairing separates chiral knot classes from their mirror images on Bring's surface.
prop:hecke-baer-star-generic:
Proposition Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) is a Baer-*-ring at generic q. Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and let q \in R be generic (not a root of unity, q \neq 1). Equip H_n(q) with the bar involution * \colon \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1} (extended antilinearly). Then H_n(q) is a Baer--ring. A self-adjoint idempotent (a projection) generates its right (resp. left) annihilator ideal.*

Failure locus — explicit characterisation

The Baer-* property fails exactly where H_n(q) ceases to be semisimple:

  H_n(q) \text{ is semisimple}
  \;\;\iff\;\;
  [k]_q \;\neq\; 0 \quad\text{for all } k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, n\},

where [k]_q := (q^k - q^{-k}) / (q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric quantum integer. The failure locus is therefore:

  \boxed{\;
    \mathrm{NonBaer}\bigl(H_n(q)\bigr)
    \;=\;
    \bigl\{\, q \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \,:\,
      q^{2k} = 1 \text{ for some } k \in \{2, \ldots, n\} \,\bigr\}.
  \;}

Equivalently, q is a primitive 2k-th root of unity for some 2 \leq k \leq n. This restricts q \in \{\zeta_4, \zeta_6, \zeta_8, \ldots, \zeta_{2n}\} (primitive forms only). At each such q, the Hoefsmit projector becomes singular and the Jacobson radical becomes non-trivial. The annihilator structure then includes nilpotent elements not generated by self-adjoint idempotents.
prf:hecke-baer-star-generic:
Proof Proof of hecke baer star generic. By the canonical Wedderburn decomposition for H_n(q) at generic q:

  H_n(q) \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} M_{d_\lambda}(R),

where d_\lambda is the dimension of the \lambda-isotypic component. Let e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) be the central primitive idempotent projecting onto the block M_{d_\lambda}(R).

Step 1 (idempotents are bar-stable). The bar involution preserves the Wedderburn block decomposition. The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i are swapped by * \colon q \mapsto q^{-1}. This permutes the symmetric and antisymmetric eigenchannels but preserves their joint span. Hence *(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} where \lambda' is the conjugate partition. For self-conjugate \lambda = \lambda' (e.g. (2,2) for n = 4), e_\lambda is itself bar-fixed. For chiral pairs (\lambda, \lambda'), the sum e_\lambda + e_{\lambda'} is bar-fixed.

Step 2 (annihilators are projection-generated). Any right ideal I \subset H_n(q) decomposes as I = \bigoplus_\lambda I_\lambda with I_\lambda \subset M_{d_\lambda}(R). For each \lambda, I_\lambda is a right ideal in the matrix algebra M_{d_\lambda}(R). Thus I_\lambda = p_\lambda M_{d_\lambda}(R) for some idempotent p_\lambda \in M_{d_\lambda}(R). The right annihilator \mathrm{Ann}_r(I) = \bigoplus_\lambda (1 - p_\lambda) M_{d_\lambda}(R) is generated by the idempotent \sum_\lambda (1 - p_\lambda).

Step 3 (idempotent self-adjointness). Each block M_{d_\lambda}(R) inherits a *-structure from H_n(q). Within M_{d_\lambda}(R), every idempotent is similar (over algebraically closed R) to a self-adjoint idempotent with respect to a chosen Hermitian form. In Hoefsmit's seminormal representation, the basis vectors of each irreducible block M_{d_\lambda}(R) are bar-orthogonal under the Frobenius trace pairing, so p_\lambda can be chosen self-adjoint.

Hence every right annihilator is generated by a self-adjoint idempotent. The left annihilator case is symmetric. \square
thm:explicit-central-idempotent-cross-ch:
Theorem The Murphy–Lagrange elements e_\lambda are the central primitive idempotents of H_n(q): sum to one, orthogonality, bar-invariance, conjugate pairing. Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field K of any characteristic at generic q (q \neq 0, not a root of unity), and let

  e_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)} \; \prod_{k=1}^{n} \; \prod_{\substack{|d| \le n-1 \\ d \neq c_T(k)}} \frac{J_k - q^{2d}}{q^{2 c_T(k)} - q^{2d}}

be the Murphy–Lagrange element attached to a partition \lambda \vdash n, built from the Jucys–Murphy elements J_1, \ldots, J_n, where c_T(k) is the content j - i of the box of T holding k and q^{2 c_T(k)} is its q-content. The inner product runs over every content d a box of a partition of n can have, so each factor is a Lagrange projector onto the eigenvalue q^{2 c_T(k)} of J_k. Let x \mapsto \overline{x} be the bar involution (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1}, antilinear) and \# the sign twist (\sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1}, q fixed). Then the four cross-checks

  1. sum-to-identity — \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} e_\lambda = 1;
  2. orthogonality — e_\lambda e_\mu = \delta_{\lambda\mu} \, e_\lambda, in particular idempotency e_\lambda^2 = e_\lambda;
  3. bar-invariance — \overline{e_\lambda} = e_\lambda for every \lambda, self-conjugate or not;
  4. conjugate pairing — \#(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} for every \lambda, so \# fixes e_\lambda exactly when \lambda = \lambda'

all hold. In particular each e_\lambda is a central idempotent, and these are the central primitive idempotents of the Wedderburn blocks.

Proof

The Wedderburn isomorphism H_n(q) \cong \prod_\lambda M_{f^\lambda}(K) sends each Murphy–Lagrange projector to a diagonal matrix unit E^\lambda_{TT}, because J_k acts on the seminormal basis vector v_S by q^{2 c_S(k)} and the content vector determines the tableau. Hence e_\lambda maps to the identity of the \lambda-block, which gives cross-checks 1 and 2 and centrality. The bar involution sends J_k to J_k^{-1} and q to q^{-1}, so it sends each projector to the Lagrange projector in J_k^{-1} with eigenvalues q^{-2d}, which picks out the same tableau (cross-check 3). The sign twist also sends J_k to J_k^{-1}, but keeps the eigenvalues q^{2d}, so it picks out the tableau with negated contents, the transpose (cross-check 4).

Status

All four cross-checks are proved on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q), for every n:

  • Cross-checks 1 and 2, and centrality. The Wedderburn isomorphism sends each Lagrange projector to a diagonal matrix unit, and the formula above, written in the multiplicative J_k, coincides with that projector.
  • Cross-check 3. Every map with the bar properties fixes every e_\lambda. No bar map is constructed; that needs a field automorphism with q \mapsto q^{-1}.
  • Cross-check 4. The sign twist is constructed from the universal property and sends e_\lambda to e_{\lambda'}.

Ground field. No hypothesis on the characteristic is needed. The Wedderburn isomorphism is built by sending each block's matrix units to Lagrange polynomials in the Jucys–Murphy elements, which needs only that distinct tableaux have distinct content vectors and that q^{2m} \neq 1 for 0 < m \le 2n. In particular the theorem holds over K = \operatorname{Frac} R[q, q^{-1}] for any integral domain R, which covers \mathbb{Q}(q) and \mathbb{F}_p(q). Over R[q, q^{-1}] itself e_\lambda is not defined, because the denominators q^{2m} - 1 are not units.

Which involution pairs \lambda with \lambda'. The bar involution fixes every e_\lambda, so \overline{e_\lambda} = e_{\lambda'} fails already at n = 2 whenever \lambda \neq \lambda'. The bar involution is the symmetry of non-abelian Stokes path reversal, whereas the sign twist pairs \lambda with \lambda' and relates the Markov trace at q to the trace at -q^{-1}.

Content range in the inner product. Taking the inner product over all admissible contents |d| \le n-1 rather than over the boxes of \lambda avoids repeated factors when two boxes on the same diagonal share a content (for example \lambda = (2,2)).
prop:explicit-central-idempotent:
Proposition Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements. The idempotency below is proved unconditionally, for every n, at generic q (The Murphy–Lagrange elements e_\lambda are the central primitive idempotents of H_n(q)).

Let H_n(q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra over a field K at generic q (q \neq 0, not a root of unity). The Jucys–Murphy elements \{J_1, \ldots, J_n\} \subset H_n(q) commute pairwise and act diagonally on the Hoefsmit seminormal basis. For any standard Young tableau T of shape \lambda \vdash n, one has J_k \cdot v_T = c_T(k; q) \cdot v_T, where

  c_T(k; q) \;=\; q^{\,2(j(k) - i(k))}

is the q-content of the box containing k at row i(k) and column j(k).

The central primitive idempotent e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) projecting onto the \lambda-Wedderburn block carries the explicit formula:

  \boxed{\;
    e_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{T \in \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)}
    \prod_{k=1}^{n}
    \prod_{\substack{c \in \mathrm{C}(n) \\ c \neq c(T(k); q)}}
    \frac{J_k - c}{c(T(k); q) - c},
  \;}

where \mathrm{C}(n) := \{c(\square; q) : \square \in \mu,\; \mu \vdash n\} comprises the distinct q-contents arising across every partition \mu \vdash n. The inner product excludes the eigenvalue c(T(k); q). Each factor forms a Lagrange-interpolation projector onto the eigenspace where J_k = c(T(k); q). This construction completely specifies Z(H_n(q)).

Cross-checks

  1. Sum-to-identity. \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} e_\lambda = 1 \in H_n(q), confirming the completeness of the partition decomposition.
  2. Orthogonality. e_\lambda e_\mu = \delta_{\lambda \mu} e_\lambda via Lagrange interpolation in commuting variables.
  3. Bar-invariance. The bar involution (\sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}, q \mapsto q^{-1}) fixes every e_\lambda, self-conjugate or not.
  4. Conjugate pairing. The sign twist (\sigma_i \mapsto -\sigma_i^{-1}) sends e_\lambda to e_{\lambda'}. The bar involution does not pair \lambda with \lambda'.

Small n examples

n \lambda conjugation class e_\lambda structure

2 (1,1) chiral pair w/ (2) \frac{L_2 - q^{2}}{q^{-2} - q^2} = \frac{q - \sigma_1}{q + q^{-1}}
3 (3) chiral pair w/ (1,1,1) q-deformed symmetriser
3 (2,1) self-conjugate standard 2D representation idempotent
4 (2,2) self-conjugate bar-fixed; witnesses \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) via depth-2 pairing with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\zeta_6)

Provenance

The Murphy-element diagonalization of Z(H_n(q)) originates with Murphy (1981, symmetric group) and Dipper–James (1986, Hecke algebra). The Lagrange-interpolation form offers the cleanest computable expression. It is standard in computer-algebra implementations of Hecke algebras.
rem:hecke-baer-star-generic-corollary:
Remark Central primitive idempotents as a complete system of bar-aware projections.

Corollary — complete system of bar-aware projections

The central primitive idempotents \{e_\lambda\}_{\lambda \vdash n} form a complete system of orthogonal projections for H_n(q), indexed by partitions of n. They are explicit (Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements) and bar-aware. Self-conjugate \lambda yield bar-fixed projections (real period witnesses). Conjugate pairs yield bar-swapped projections (chirality-twisted witnesses).
rem:chirality-period-pairing:
Remark Chirality structure on Goncharov period classes via the bar involution. The bar involution * \colon q \mapsto q^{-1} on H_n(q) (equivalently, the Hecke algebra antipode *(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i^{-1}) acts on the central primitive idempotents e_\lambda by partition conjugation: *(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'}, where \lambda' denotes the transposed Young diagram (Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements Cross-check 3-4).

Conditional on the conjectural correspondence between Gröbner--Shirshov filtration depth and Goncharov period depth, together with Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) is a Baer-*-ring at generic q, this bar action categorifies the chirality structure of hyperbolic 3-manifold volumes:

Self-conjugate (\lambda = \lambda') *(e_\lambda) = e_\lambda amphichiral knot \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{K}) — real period in \mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R})
Chiral pair (\lambda \neq \lambda') *(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda'} chiral knot K \neq \overline{K} \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{K}), \mathrm{CS}(K) = -\mathrm{CS}(\overline{K}) — period with a Tate twist

The figure-8 row

The knot 4_1 is amphichiral: 4_1 \cong \overline{4_1}. Its dominant cell in H_4(q) is \lambda = (2, 2), the unique self-conjugate 4-partition. The bar-fixed projection e_{(2,2)} yields the real period 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \in \mathbb{R} without a Tate twist.

A chiral example: trefoil

The knot 3_1 is chiral: 3_1 \neq \overline{3_1}. Its dominant cell \lambda = (3) pairs with \lambda' = (1, 1, 1) under the bar involution: *(e_{(3)}) = e_{(1, 1, 1)}. The volume vanishes (the trefoil is not hyperbolic), but the Chern–Simons invariant \mathrm{CS}(3_1) = \pm \pi^2 / 6 flips sign under the bar involution. This yields the chirality-twisted depth-3 period in \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2. It manifests the same chirality structure at depth 3.

Compatibility with the depth filtration

The bar involution preserves the iterated-integral depth filtration: * \colon G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \to G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q). Each depth G^{(n)} decomposes into bar-eigenspaces:

  G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \;=\; G^{(n), +} \;\oplus\; G^{(n), -},

where G^{(n), \pm} are the \pm 1 eigenspaces of *. Under the archimedean completion \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}:

  • G^{(n), +} \to \mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{R}) produces real periods.
  • G^{(n), -} \to i \cdot \mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{R}) produces imaginary periods. Geometrically, these correspond to Chern–Simons-style invariants paired with a (2\pi i)^n-factor from the Tate motive.

Each Goncharov period class \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} inherits a bar-grading. Hyperbolic volume resides in \mathcal{P}_2^+, Chern–Simons in \mathcal{P}_3^-, and multiple polylog values split according to the amphichirality of the underlying motive.

Provenance

The bar involution's role remains structural. It organises period classes by the orientation-reversal symmetry of the motivic base ring.

Falsifiability

One proposes a test using a chiral hyperbolic knot K with known \mathrm{CS}(K) \neq 0. The simplest such knot is 5_2, which has \mathrm{Vol} \approx 2.8281 and \mathrm{CS} \approx -0.1530\,\pi^2 \pmod{\pi^2}. One verifies three points:

  1. The dominant cell of 5_2 in H_4(q) (or H_5(q)) forms a chiral pair, rather than a self-conjugate cell.
  2. The depth-2 pairing produces the real \mathrm{Vol}(5_2).
  3. The depth-3 pairing on the same cell produces the chirality-twisted \mathrm{CS}(5_2).

Discharge remains open. The cell identification at H_5(q) presents the primary technical obstacle.
rem:bring-embeddable-knots:
Remark Bring-embeddable knots: genus-bounded table and per-knot witness targets for the depth correspondence. The QOU aether selects the knots whose Seifert genus is bounded by Bring's surface genus (Complete decomposition of the tensor tower, Exhaustiveness of the QOU knots in the Descartes space (open)):

  \mathrm{Knots}_{\mathrm{Bring}}
  \;:=\;

By the generation completeness theorem, a finite list of torus-knot generators combined with skein crossing changes generates this class. The recursive atom-knot atlas lists the canonical low-genus representatives.

Genus stratification and generators

The full enumeration of Bring-embeddable knots by genus appears in Table: Bring-embeddable knot table. Every Bring-embeddable knot derives from seven torus-knot generators:

For each Bring-embeddable knot K with dominant cell \lambda_K in H_n(q) and shape parameter z_K \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times:

prop:mobius-energy:
Proposition Categorical recovery of Möbius energy. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (Definition) with aether parameter q (Definition), categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q (Definition), and q-Hodge star \star_q (Definition).

Let \varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A) be a smooth closed curve (a knot embedding) and let \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) denote the categorical mass (Definition).

Define the categorical Möbius energy by

  E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  = 
  \int_A \!\circ \mathrm{tr}_A \!\iint_{S^1 \times S^1 \setminus \mathrm{diag}}
  \!\!\Bigl(
    \Delta(\varrho(s)) \otimes \Delta(\varrho(t))
  \Bigr)
  \star_q
  \Bigl\lVert
    \frac{d\varrho}{ds} \wedge_q \frac{d\varrho}{dt}
  \Bigr\rVert
  ds dt,

where \Delta is the Hopf comultiplication, \int_A is the Frobenius form (Remark), and the integration excludes the diagonal \mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1.

In the classical limit q \to 1, the categorical Möbius energy recovers the classical Möbius energy up to a topological normalization:

  \lim_{q \to 1} E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  = 
  \frac{1}{4} E(\varrho)
  +  \text{const}.

The additive constant is not determined by the construction. Shifting E_{\mathrm{cat}} by any real a shifts \text{const} by a while preserving both the Möbius invariance of E_{\mathrm{cat}} and the relation itself, so every real value of \text{const} is realised and no single value holds across instances. Reading \text{const} as a topological normalisation, a quantity determined by the knot type of \varrho alone, requires further structure fixing the additive zero of E_{\mathrm{cat}}, which the definition above does not supply. What is established here is the shape of the classical limit: the categorical energy is an affine function of the classical Möbius energy with slope 1/4.

Here E(\varrho) is the classical Möbius energy

  E(\varrho)
  = 
  \iint_{S^1 \times S^1}
  \Bigl(
    \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
    - 
    \frac{1}{D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))^2}
  \Bigr)
  \lvert \varrho'(s) \rvert  \lvert \varrho'(t) \rvert
  ds dt,

where D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t)) denotes the intrinsic arc-length distance along \varrho.

Lemma Classical limit of the Frobenius--Hopf kernel is the repulsive 1/r^2. Let \gamma be a knot filament and K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t) = \mathrm{tr}\bigl(\Delta(\gamma(s)) \otimes \Delta(\gamma(t))\bigr) the Frobenius--Hopf kernel. Assume two reductions:

  1. (Hodge-star reduction) as q \to 1, K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t) converges to the classical kernel K_{\mathrm{Kill}}(s, t) of the Frobenius pairing \int_A \circ \mu;
  2. (Killing-form reduction) at q = 1 that pairing is the standard \mathrm{SU}(2) Killing form, and K_{\mathrm{Kill}}(s, t) = 1 / \lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2 for \gamma(s) \neq \gamma(t).

Then the Frobenius--Hopf kernel collapses to the repulsive 1/r^2:

  K_{\mathrm{FH}}(q; s, t)
  \xrightarrow{q \to 1}
  \frac{1}{\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2}.

Neither reduction is proved here; both are hypotheses.
